title: OC-Distill: Ontology-aware Contrastive Learning with Cross-Modal Distillation for ICU Risk Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2604.16878v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Early prediction of severe clinical deterioration and remaining length of stay can enable timely intervention and better resource allocation in high-acuity settings such as the ICU. This has driven the development of machine learning models that leverage continuous streams of vital signs and other physiological signals for real-time risk prediction. Despite their promise, existing methods have important limitations. Contrastive pretraining treats all patients as equally strong negatives, failing to capture clinically meaningful similarity between patients with related diagnoses. Meanwhile, downstream fine-tuning typically ignores complementary modalities such as clinical notes, which provide rich contextual information unavailable in physiological signals alone. To address these challenges, we propose OC-Distill, a two-stage framework that leverages multimodal supervision during training while requiring only vital signs at inference.

translated_title: OC-Distill：面向ICU风险预测的本体感知对比学习与跨模态蒸馏
translated_abstract: 早期预测严重临床恶化和剩余住院时间，可以在ICU等高敏锐度环境中实现及时干预和更好的资源分配。这推动了利用连续生命体征和其他生理信号流进行实时风险预测的机器学习模型的发展。尽管这些方法前景广阔，但现有方法存在重要局限性。对比预训练将所有患者视为同等强度的负样本，未能捕捉到相关诊断患者之间的临床意义相似性。同时，下游微调通常忽略互补模态，如临床笔记，这些笔记提供了仅凭生理信号无法获得的丰富上下文信息。为解决这些挑战，我们提出了OC-Distill，一个两阶段框架，在训练期间利用多模态监督，而在推理时仅需要生命体征。
tldr: 本文提出OC-Distill框架，通过本体感知对比学习和跨模态蒸馏，在训练时利用多模态信息，推理时仅需生命体征，以改进ICU风险预测。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes OC-Distill, a framework that leverages ontology-aware contrastive learning and cross-modal distillation to use multimodal supervision during training while requiring only vital signs at inference, improving ICU risk prediction.
